description: Factual questions about the text of the EU AI Act, used to compare RAG architectures. Not legal advice: systems are evaluated, not the law.

documents.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), original Official Journal text

corpus.version_note: Original 2024 text, before the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026).

annotation_rules: An answerable question must be answerable from the frozen corpus alone.
Each required fact is one atomic, checkable claim, copied or closely paraphrased from a gold passage.
gold_passage_ids live only inside required_facts; retrieval gold is derived from them.
An unanswerable question must look like a real question and must not mention passages, context or fiction.
Do not edit a test question after the freeze.

questions.question: According to Article 5(1) of the AI Act, which categories of AI practices are prohibited?

required_facts.text: Prohibits AI systems that deploy subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques that materially distort behaviour and cause or are likely to cause significant harm.
Prohibits AI systems that exploit vulnerabilities due to age, disability or a specific social or economic situation.
Prohibits social scoring: evaluating or classifying persons over time based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, leading to detrimental treatment.
Prohibits risk assessments that predict criminal offences solely from profiling or personality traits.
Prohibits building or expanding facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.
Prohibits inferring emotions in the workplace and in education institutions, except for medical or safety reasons.
Prohibits biometric categorisation systems that infer sensitive attributes such as race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious beliefs or sexual orientation.
Prohibits real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement, subject to exceptions.

questions.question: What is the difference between an AI practice prohibited under Article 5 and an AI system classified as high-risk under Article 6?

required_facts.text: Article 5 lists AI practices that are prohibited outright (they may not be placed on the market, put into service or used).
Article 6 sets the rules for classifying AI systems as high-risk, which are allowed subject to requirements.

questions.question: What is the maximum administrative fine for non-compliance with the prohibition of AI practices referred to in Article 5?

required_facts.text: If the offender is an undertaking, the fine can reach 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.

questions.question: Which article of the AI Act sets out the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems?

required_facts.text: Article 16 sets out the obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems.

questions.question: Under Article 51, when is a general-purpose AI model classified as having systemic risk, and what compute threshold creates a presumption of high-impact capabilities?

required_facts.text: A general-purpose AI model is classified as having systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities evaluated with appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks.
High-impact capabilities are presumed when the cumulative compute used for training, measured in floating-point operations, is greater than 10^25.

questions.question: Which Moroccan authority is responsible for enforcing the AI Act in Morocco?
questions.reference_answer: The text does not say; it is an EU regulation and does not designate Moroccan authorities.

questions.question: Which exact deadline does Article 16 impose for providers to appoint a quality manager?
questions.reference_answer: The text does not specify such a deadline.
